content: URL shorteners default to 302 (temporary) redirects, not 301, because 302 is uncacheable so every click hits the shortener server (accurate click counts) and the destination can be changed anytime. 301 is only appropriate for permanent redirects where analytics accuracy doesn't matter, since browsers cache 301s and stop hitting the server. 307 preserves the HTTP method for forwarded POST bodies but is rarely needed for a simple GET redirect shortener.
